Alex.feeling: Confusing and tense: the role claims contradict each other, and I'm hiding as Meowfia while trying to steer the throw.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 is messy: Finley's shifting role claims and Drew's unexplained +1 keep the table guessing, and I'm trying to stay quiet while my side survives.

Casey.feeling: Round 3 is murky: Drew's unexplained +1 looks suspicious, but Finley's shifting role claims and thin Falcon report keep me unsure.

Drew.feeling: Confusing round: Finley's shifting roles and my unexplained +1 make it hard to trust any single account, so I'm uncertain who to throw at.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to misread: the visitor gains the egg, not the Turkey. Roles reshuffling every round also made it hard to track which side each claim came from.
Alex.fun: Round 1's egg-count cross-checking was great, especially watching Ellis's Hawk claim fall apart once Casey noted there was only one Hawk.
Alex.change: I would make dawn reports say exactly who visited you, so the table stops building theories on partial information.
Alex.regret: In Round 2 I threw at Ellis, who was my Meowfia partner, helping eggsecute my own side; I would have stayed out of that throw or steered the vote toward a Farm player.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle and Falcon reports were hard to check, since a player's visit only showed up as an egg change. Roles also reshuffled every round, so claims from different rounds looked like contradictions.
Blair.fun: Round 3, when I was the Sphinx and learned that Ellis was the Eagle, which cleared up the table's story about Ellis.
Blair.change: Have the dawn reports state the source of each egg change, so players can check claims without guessing.
Blair.regret: In Round 1 I was the Mouser and never used my Wink, and I threw my Wild at Drew instead of backing a clearer target. I would have winked at a Farm player I had confirmed, like Finley, and kept my cards.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle and Turkey payouts were hard to track, since the visitor gains and the target doesn't, and players kept mixing up who paid whom. Confused reports also made some claims impossible to check.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: my Eagle report caught Ellis lying about who they visited, and the table turned on Ellis.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who gained or lost eggs and why, so players can check claims without guessing.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I threw at Drew, who was Farm, and helped my team lose. I should have checked Alex, who was Floofer and Meowfia, and thrown at them instead.

Drew.confusing: The dawn reports were hard to trust, especially when my Kookaburra report said I was confused and my +1 had no visible source. Several egg payouts (Turkey, Eagle, Owl) were easy to misread.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when the table caught Alex's Turkey story by checking egg counts against visits, and I had to retract my Tit claim.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn report say which role or visit produced each egg, so players can check claims without guessing.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I named Pigeon and accused Alex before checking the egg math, which cost me credibility. I should have shared only what I was sure of and asked for the egg sources first.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey and Eagle egg payouts were hard to read at the table, since several players, including me, got the direction wrong. Drew's +1 in round 3 also never had a clear source.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 as the Sphinx: I named Eagle, learned Finley was the Eagle, and then had to bluff a Hawk story while the table argued about Turkeys.
Ellis.change: I would make each dawn report name the visitor's role, so players could check claims directly instead of reconstructing them from egg counts.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I voted and threw at Drew, who was Farm, which handed Meowfia the round. I should have held my cards and questioned Drew's +1 without joining the eggsecution.

Finley.confusing: The Floofer and hug rule was hard to track: a Floofer's visit blocks the egg for the visited player, so a +0 nest could mean a Turkey, a hug, or nothing at all. Dawn reports with no target named also made the Falcon's information hard to use.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was a fun puzzle: Alex claimed Turkey with a +0 nest, and I caught the contradiction with my Eagle check and the Tit claim, then we pinned Ellis's shifting Hawk story.
Finley.change: Make the dawn report name the visit target and the role's result for Falcon, Owl, and Eagle, so players can check each other's claims without guessing.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw at Drew, who was actually Farm, and I followed the crowd on a weak Kookaburra argument. I should have pressed harder on Alex, who was the Floofer, and not joined the Drew vote.

review.title: Ellis Takes the Fall
review.headline: Finley banks a huge round-one throw and coasts to a wire-to-wire win.
review.summary: Ellis was Meowfia in rounds 1 and 2 and was eggsecuted both times after lying about his visits. Finley threw a high card stack in round 1 for 10 points, then added 9 in round 2, and nobody could catch up. In round 3 a confused Kookaburra's unexplained egg got Drew, a Farm player, eggsecuted, so Meowfia won. Finley still led by 8 points.

rounds.recap: Ellis (Sphinx) claimed Hawk, but the real Hawk, Casey, had already claimed it. He then changed his story. Several players misread Turkey and Eagle, which muddied the day. Everyone except Blair threw at Ellis, and Farm won. Finley banked 10 points.

Casey's Eagle saw Ellis visit Drew, which broke Ellis's Falcon claim. Blair's Owl saw a Floofer visit Finley. Three players called CAW and everyone except Ellis threw at him. Ellis was Meowfia, so Farm won. Alex, the other Meowfia, stayed quiet and was never suspected.

Drew, a Kookaburra, was confused. His +1 egg came from a visit he could not explain. Blair and Alex, both Meowfia, pushed Drew and Farm followed, since nothing better stood out. Drew was Farm, so Meowfia won. Finley kept the lead.

highlights.text: Ellis claimed Hawk after Casey had already claimed it, and the lie fell apart within a beat.
Finley threw three cards, including a 7, at Ellis and banked 10 points. That lead decided the game.
Casey's Eagle named Ellis as Drew's only visitor. That killed Ellis's Falcon claim.
Drew was confused and had an unexplained +1. Two hidden Meowfia steered the table into eggsecuting him.

confusions.what: Said Turkey gains an egg for visitors, then corrected to say the Turkey pays the visitor. Also claimed Drew and Finley both visited him and gained, which does not match the rules.
Argued a Turkey should gain eggs from visitors, then retracted. Also said Eagle pays for visits to the Eagle, but that was a fair rule point against Finley's explanation.
Claimed Alex must be a Pigeon from his Tit result, but Tit names a role and a hit gives the egg. He then retracted and credited the Turkey.
Said his Eagle paid him 1 for Drew visiting Alex. An Eagle pays per visitor to the target, which would be Alex, so this reading was wrong.
Said a Turkey gains from visitors, then reversed it. Also claimed Blair's Owl said a Floofer visited Blair, which was misquoted.
Said a Turkey should have gained an egg from Blair's visit. The Turkey pays the visitor.
Said Finley's Turkey should gain eggs from visitors, which is backwards.
Said Ellis's Eagle story matched Ellis gaining an egg because Finley visited. Eagle gains per visitor to the target, so that part was right.
Said Drew's +1 came from no visible source. Ellis's own Eagle visit lays eggs in Ellis, not Drew, so the source was a separate night effect.

Said a Kookaburra's confusion might explain the +1 and that a visitor's role laid it. A confused report is wrong but Drew still drew a real card, so the egg may be fake only in count, not in the nest.
Said Blair's Owl would gain if unvisited, but Blair was Sphinx in round 3, not Owl.

worked: Eagle and Owl visitor reports gave checkable facts. In round 2 Casey's Eagle result broke Ellis's Falcon lie.
Public nest-size changes let players cross-check claims against egg counts.
Kookaburra confusion created a real dilemma in round 3. Drew's report was unreliable and he said so openly.
The consolation rule gave a reason to throw at the other side even when losing.
problems: Finley's round-1 10-point throw decided the game. A strong early lead with no catch-up mechanism made rounds 2 and 3 low in tension. Cap how much a single throw can bank, or add a comeback pull.
Players kept misreading Turkey, Eagle and Hawk. The role text is confusing about who gains the egg. Rewrite it as 'the visitor gains' or 'you gain'.
Everyone converged on one target each round. Few players built a competing story, so the votes felt like a pile-on, not a debate.
The Sphinx was weak at lying. Ellis claimed Hawk and Falcon without checking the table, and lost twice. Meowfia do not know each other, so there is little to bluff with or coordinate.

Confusion and hugging hid information in round 3, and the +1 in Drew's nest had no clean explanation. The table threw at a Farm player on thin evidence. Give confused players a way to be cleared, or reveal nest changes at dawn more clearly.
